text:
laura: Quick question — for the new gateway routing rules, what's our intended precedence when JWT claims, an X-Customer-Priority header, and User-Agent heuristics all suggest different routes?

james: I was assuming JWT claims > signed customer header > UA heuristics. Claims are authoritative for tenancy.

laura: ok that matches my gut, but two followups: (1) how do we validate the signed header? (2) do we ever let UA override a claim for fallback?

kai: For (1) we should require X-RW-SIGN (HMAC) + X-RW-TIMESTAMP and verify against org key in KMS. Reject if timestamp drift > 5m. For (2) UA should only be used for best-effort routing when auth info is missing — not to override a valid claim.

maria: concern: UA heuristics can cause cache fragmentation and telemetry noise. If we route by UA for fallbacks, add a metric tag like `route_reason=ua_fallback` so we can monitor.

laura: good point. also want to avoid header spoofing attacks. kai, can you paste a minimal matcher config we can review?

kai: yeah — here's a draft matcher block we prototyped in the router: 

```yaml
- match: 
    - condition: jwt.claims.org_id != null
      action: route_to: tenant-shard-{jwt.claims.org_id}
    - condition: header.X-RW-SIGN && header.X-RW-TIMESTAMP && verify_signature(header.X-RW-SIGN)
      action: route_to: tenant-shard-{header.X-Customer-Id}
    - condition: user_agent matches /redwood-app\/([0-9]+\.)?\/
      action: route_to: ua-optimized-pool
    - default: route_to: shared-pool
```

kai: verify_signature() is a logical op — implementation calls our kms service to validate HMAC using the org key.

james: we should also normalize headers (lowercase keys, trim spaces) before evaluating. Some SDKs send weird spacing in X-Customer-Id.

maria: add to config: a whitelist of headers we accept for routing, e.g. ["x-customer-id","x-rw-sign","authorization","user-agent"]. Drop others for routing decisions. Plus rate-limit signed-header paths more strictly.

sam: telemetry + rollout note: when we flip the precedence we should run a canary for 1% traffic with `route_reason=jwt_priority` and check error rate, auth failures, and cache hit ratio. Also export a counter `routing_decision{rule="jwt|signed|ua|default"}`.

laura: agreed. also need an ops playbook for signature failures — don't silently route to shared-pool for signed-header failures. Return 401 or 403 depending on failure type. We had an outage once where ambiguous fallback caused cross-tenant noise.

kai: +1 on strict failure semantics. For signature ttl: allow replay window of 5 minutes, store short-lived nonces only if we want replay protection. For now we'll log `signature_failure_reason` with sampling.

infra-bot: deploy check — router-config PR #847 currently failing lint: missing `whitelist_headers` field.

laura: thanks infra-bot, i'll patch the PR.

james: tiny UX ask for Console: when a route is chosen, show the `route_reason` on the request detail page so SREs can debug quickly.

maria: and surface the header normalization applied (e.g., `x-customer-id: trimmed, lowercased`) in the audit log.

laura: OK steps: 1) kai will add KMS signature verification + whitelist + explicit failure codes. 2) sam will add metrics counters & canary pipeline. 3) james + product will add the route_reason to Console. 4) maria will write a short ops guide for signature failures and UA fallbacks.

kai: starting a branch now — i'll include unit tests for signature verification and a small fuzz test for UA patterns.

maria: will set up dashboards: routing_decision distribution, signature_failure_reason, ua_fallback_rate, cache_hit_by_route.

laura: thanks team. let's avoid making UA the default unless all other signals are absent. We'll iterate after canary. :thumbsup:
